title: ECMP lever row claims 3 wides carry base demand; its own numbers say they cannot
location: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/surge-explainer/surge-explainer.html — Section B, 'The levers that do exist' table (ECMP row) vs 'Ranked, for this exact screenshot' table (row 3)
evidence: Base demand through one bundle = 6 arrivals/tick = 180 u/s (4×30 + 2×30). Split across 3 equal-cost wides: 60 u/s each = 2 packets/tick — under the 1.33/tick service of one wide; with ECMP the load lands on whichever bundle is on the hash. … Through one bundle, base demand is 6 arrivals/tick = 180 u/s (4×30 + 2×30). A pair of parallel wides = 80 u/s ≈ 2.7 packets/tick — meaningful but not enough for base demand alone (that needs ~180 u/s ≈ 4–5 wides through one pair).

recommended_fix: Rewrite the row: base demand needs ≥5 equal-cost wides (≤36 u/s each, under each wide's 40 u/s service); align with the ranked table's '4–5 wides'.

title: 'the sim ticks at 20 Hz, so u/s = u per tick' — the stated tick rate contradicts the stated unit equivalence
evidence:
A packet costs 30 u to cross one edge; a pipe's u/s is how many it provides per second (the sim ticks at 20 Hz, so u/s = u per tick). Transit time per hop = ceil(30 ÷ capacity): narrow (5 u/s) = 6 ticks (0.3 s), standard (15) = 2 ticks (0.1 s), wide (40) = 1 tick. …
= 60 s @ 20 Hz logic
detail: At the artifact's own 20 Hz ('tick 1200 = 60 s'), one second is 20 ticks, so u/s would be 20× u/tick. The transit math consumes capacity per tick; the 'so' clause is inverted.
recommended_fix: State that catalog capacities labeled u/s are consumed as u-per-tick by the engine, or delete the false justification clause.
